pdf_note: NASA NTRS PDF; Figure 11 is an embedded raster image (about 220 ppi)

x_axis.note: vertical grid lines at slope 0 and 16 deg (grid lines every 2 deg agree, 68.8 px per deg)

y_axis.note: horizontal grid lines at wheel slip 10 and 80 percent (grid lines every 10 percent agree, 8.21 px per percent)

meta.source_title: Effect of Angle of Attack on Slope Climbing Performance (Creager, Jones, Smith; NASA/TM 2017-219549, December 2017)
meta.evidence_row: TM3-001 to TM3-007 (same source, other findings)
meta.figure_or_table: Figure 11, angle of attack 90 deg (orange diamonds)
meta.x_name: slope angle (actual, best fit plane of the surface point cloud)
meta.vehicle: Scarab rover, 400 kg, four rigid wheels, active suspension not used (fixed chassis height and axle spacing), wheel speed 0.13 rad/s for 30 s
meta.soil: GRC-1 lunar simulant sand mixture, loosened (Table 1: D60 0.390 mm, specific gravity 2.583, relative density 11 percent, cohesion about 0 kPa)
meta.preparation: SLOPE laboratory tilt bed about 6 m by 4.5 m, GRC-1 23 cm deep, loosened before each test; mean cone index gradient 2.5 plus or minus 0.5 kPa/mm
meta.comparability_note: Slip of the rear wheel averaged over each 30 s run from photogrammetric wheel tracking, i = 1 minus distance travelled over (effective radius times wheel rotation) in the direction the vehicle faced; front and rear differ by less than 0.5 percent (text). x values are the actual slope angles of each run read from the figure, single runs (no repeats). The 0 deg reference test, plotted at about minus 1 percent for all four series, is left out because the four markers overlap there. Markers found automatically as connected colour components after removing the connecting lines by morphological opening. load_per_wheel_N derived here as 400 kg times 9.81 divided by 4 wheels (the text says the load was fairly even on flat ground). GRC-1 is a manufactured sand mixture with lunar strength properties, wider graded than dune sand; very large and heavy wheels. CAUTION: the 90 deg angle of attack runs are probably the same Scarab tests as inotsume2016_fig3_9_scarab_direct_ascent (same vehicle, tilt bed, soil and period); do not pool the two curves as independent data.
